clusters.headline: President Zelenskyy Criticizes SpaceX Over Starshield Speed Restrictions in Ukraine
clusters.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused SpaceX of imposing political speed restrictions on Starshield satellite terminals operating over Russian-occupied territories. Zelenskyy stated that these limits, which cap speeds at 161 kph, have hindered Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones and conduct military strikes. While SpaceX reportedly claims the issues are technical, Ukrainian officials maintain the restrictions are deliberate and undermine national sovereignty. The limitations have been reported by the Ukrainian government for five consecutive days as of November 13.

clusters.headline: Bomb discovered at Peoria, Illinois ethanol plant prompts mandatory evacuations
clusters.summary: Authorities discovered a bomb at the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, on Friday, triggering a mandatory one-mile evacuation zone. The evacuation order affected residents and businesses in both Peoria and the adjacent municipality of East Peoria. While bomb technicians rendered the initial device safe on Friday evening, police and the FBI continue to search the facility for additional threats. Peoria Mayor Rita Ali and Police Chief Brad Dixon confirmed the device was a credible threat, and the evacuation order remained in place as of Saturday.

clusters.headline: United States Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years
clusters.summary: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has revoked the United States' measles-elimination status after determining the country failed to halt continuous transmission of the virus for over a year. This decision ends a 26-year period during which the U.S. was considered measles-free. Reports indicate the country is currently facing its highest number of measles cases in over three decades, with figures ranging from 5,412 to 7,500 confirmed cases in 2026. The surge is attributed to declining vaccination rates, policy changes, and staff cuts.

clusters.headline: Paraguayan Prosecutors Charge Former President Santiago Peña Following Ueno Bank Collapse
clusters.summary: Paraguayan authorities have charged former President Santiago Peña with criminal association, adding to existing charges of breach of trust and self-dealing. The charges follow his impeachment and removal from office by the Senate on November 6, 2024, amid a national financial crisis triggered by the collapse of the digital lender Ueno. Prosecutors allege that Peña used his position to direct millions in public funds to the bank, which held savings for nearly half the country's population. Peña is currently held in pretrial detention at a military facility, while Vice-President Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as his successor.

Ueno bank held approximately $800 million in public funds.

clusters.headline: German Parliament Approves Expanded Powers for Intelligence Agencies
clusters.summary: The German Bundestag passed legislation on Friday granting the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) and the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) significantly expanded operational powers. The new law allows agencies to conduct cyberattacks on foreign systems, manipulate data, enter homes, and use AI for biometric analysis. Additionally, the reform permits the recruitment of informants as young as 16 in exceptional cases. The bill, supported by the governing Christian Democrats and Social Democrats, aims to counter espionage, terrorism, and sabotage, though it faced opposition from the AfD and the Left Party.
key_facts: The legislation passed with 308 votes in favor, 190 against, and 71 abstentions.
Agencies are authorized to disable systems and destroy physical weapons like drones.

clusters.headline: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and President Trump Agree to 90-Day SNAP Rule Delay
clusters.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has secured a 90-day extension for small retailers nationwide to comply with new Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) food-stocking requirements. The agreement, reached following discussions with President Donald Trump and Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, delays the original November 4 deadline. The new USDA guidelines require stores to stock at least seven varieties of items within four staple food categories: dairy, grains, protein, and fruits or vegetables. The extension takes effect on Friday and aims to prevent small businesses, such as bodegas and corner stores, from losing their ability to accept food stamps.
